description: A two-panel explanatory schematic (no data axes, no numeric scales) contrasting dislocation glide reversibility in two conditions. Both panels depict horizontal glide planes drawn as lines decorated with regular vertical tick marks (obstacles/atomic rows), with thick black arrows above and below labelled τc (applied shear stress) pointing in opposite directions to indicate load reversal. (a) "ST condition", on a cream background: a blue filled circle labelled "SRO" marks a short-range-ordered region intersected by the upper glide plane; on the lower plane two red dashed circles enclose dislocation symbols — one crossed and offset from the plane (a path not retraced) and one clustered — annotated in red "Localized absence of SRO" and "Premature destruction of SRO"; orange text below the box reads "Low slip reversibility". (b) "Aged condition", on a pale violet background: a green rounded rectangle labelled "Intragranular κ" intersects both the upper and lower glide planes, with small arrows showing dislocations meeting the κ-carbide; purple text below the box reads "High slip reversibility". Together the panels argue that premature SRO destruction in the ST sample localises strain, whereas the uniform κ-carbide dispersion in the aged sample enables path-retracing. No numeric values are printed.

observations.observation: The figure is a two-panel schematic (not a data plot): panel (a) is headed "ST condition" and panel (b) is headed "Aged condition".

Both panels draw a horizontal glide plane as a straight line with evenly spaced vertical tick marks, with thick black arrows above and below the plane labelled τc pointing in opposite directions, representing forward and reverse loading.
In panel (a) a blue filled circle labelled "SRO" sits on the upper glide plane, marking a short-range-ordered region intersecting the slip plane.

Panel (a) contains red annotation text "Localized absence of SRO" and "Premature destruction of SRO" above two red dashed circles on the lower glide plane that enclose dislocation symbols, one of which is drawn crossed and displaced from the plane.
Panel (b) shows a green rounded rectangle labelled "Intragranular κ" intersecting both the upper and lower drawn glide planes, with small arrows indicating dislocation interaction with the κ-carbide.
Panel (a) is captioned below in orange with "Low slip reversibility" and panel (b) below in purple with "High slip reversibility".
No numeric values, axis scales, scale bars or legends are printed anywhere in either panel.
The caption states that Fig. 12 is a schematic diagram showing the difference in slip reversibility in the ST (a) and aged (b) samples.

The citing text states that in the ST sample planar slip bands are attributed to the SRO structure in the austenitic matrix and that repeated shearing destroys the SRO prematurely, producing non-uniform softening and local strain concentrations (Fig. 12a).
The citing text states that aging induces coherent ordered L1₂-structured intragranular κ-carbides that amplify glide plane softening through APB formation and suppress cross-slip (Fig. 12b).
The citing text states that in aged samples dislocations more readily retrace their path on well-defined softened planes during load reversal, reducing accumulated damage per cycle.
The schematic's crossed-out dislocation symbol on the lower glide plane of panel (a) is the only pictogram that directly depicts a dislocation failing to retrace its path.

subfigures.description: Schematic of the ST (solution-treated) condition: a horizontal glide plane with tick-marked obstacles, black τc arrows above and below pointing in opposite senses, a blue circle labelled "SRO" on the upper plane, and two red dashed circles on the lower plane containing dislocation symbols (one crossed/offset), annotated in red "Localized absence of SRO" and "Premature destruction of SRO"; orange label below reads "Low slip reversibility".

Schematic of the aged condition: two horizontal glide planes with tick-marked obstacles, black τc arrows above and below pointing in opposite senses, and a green rounded rectangle labelled "Intragranular κ" intersecting both planes with small up/down arrows; purple label below reads "High slip reversibility".
